quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Cash Flow, Budgets, and Buffers
quizzes.intro: Check whether you understand cash flow, realistic budgeting, needs versus wants, and emergency savings.

questions.prompt: What is cash flow in personal finance?

options.text: Only the money in your investment account
Money in minus money out over a period
A guaranteed monthly profit from budgeting
Your credit score expressed as dollars

questions.explanation: Cash flow measures income versus spending over time and shows whether you can build buffers or are falling behind.

wrongExplanations.a: Investments are assets; cash flow is about inflows and outflows.
wrongExplanations.d: Credit scores are separate from cash flow.

questions.prompt: Why should irregular annual expenses be converted to monthly averages in a budget?

options.text: Because banks legally require it
So predictable ‘surprises’ are funded before they hit
Because irregular expenses do not count as spending
To guarantee investment returns

questions.explanation: Averaging irregular costs into monthly plans prevents false surpluses and creates sinking funds.

wrongExplanations.a: This is a planning practice, not a legal banking rule.
wrongExplanations.c: Irregular expenses still use real money.
wrongExplanations.d: Budgeting averages are unrelated to guaranteed returns—which do not exist here.

questions.prompt: Which approach best describes a budget that survives real life?

options.text: Assume you will never spend on enjoyment
Track real patterns, set ambitious-but-usable limits, and automate savings
Copy a stranger’s viral spreadsheet without changes
Ignore tracking because intuition is enough

questions.explanation: Realistic budgets start from actual behavior, leave room for living, and use automation.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of an emergency fund?

options.text: Funding vacations without guilt
Covering unexpected necessary expenses and income shocks
Guaranteeing stock market gains
Replacing the need for any insurance

questions.explanation: Emergency funds provide liquid resilience for true shocks, not lifestyle spending.

wrongExplanations.a: Vacations belong in sinking funds or discretionary savings.
wrongExplanations.c: Cash buffers do not guarantee market returns.
wrongExplanations.d: Insurance still covers catastrophic risks differently.

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects a healthy money mindset from this lesson?

options.text: Every dollar spent on enjoyment is a moral failure
Money is a tool for safety, freedom, and values-based choices within trade-offs
Guaranteed-return schemes are the fastest responsible path
Net worth equals personal worth

questions.explanation: The lesson treats money as a tool with trade-offs, not shame or hype.

wrongExplanations.a: Values-based wants can be planned without shame.
wrongExplanations.c: Guaranteed-return promises are rejected as hype.
wrongExplanations.d: Financial metrics are not identity scores.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Debt, Credit, and Saving Goals
quizzes.intro: Apply debt strategy, credit basics, sinking funds, and decision discipline.

questions.prompt: What is the avalanche debt method?

options.text: Paying whichever bill feels luckiest
Putting extra payments toward the highest interest rate first
Ignoring minimum payments to free cash
Investing rent money to outpace interest

questions.explanation: Avalanche prioritizes the costliest debt mathematically while maintaining other minimums.

wrongExplanations.a: Random focus is not a method.
wrongExplanations.c: Skipping minimums risks fees and credit damage.
wrongExplanations.d: Using essential money for speculation is dangerous.

questions.prompt: Why can paying only minimums on high-interest revolving debt be problematic?

options.text: Because minimums are illegal
Because balances can linger for years while interest costs pile up
Because minimums raise your salary
Because minimums guarantee a perfect credit score

questions.explanation: Minimums keep accounts current but can make payoff slow and expensive.

wrongExplanations.a: Minimums are allowed; they are just often inefficient.
wrongExplanations.d: Credit outcomes depend on broader behavior.

questions.prompt: What are sinking funds best used for?

options.text: Gambling on tips
Planned irregular expenses like premiums, travel, or device replacement
Replacing all insurance forever
Hiding spending from yourself

questions.explanation: Sinking funds turn expected irregular costs into monthly savings so they are not emergencies.

wrongExplanations.a: Speculation is not a sinking fund purpose.
wrongExplanations.c: Insurance remains important for catastrophic risk.
wrongExplanations.d: Good sinking funds increase clarity, not secrecy.

questions.prompt: Which habit most reliably helps everyday financial control?

options.text: Automating savings and bill payments on payday
Checking social media lifestyles for targets
Waiting until a crisis to look at statements
Memorizing get-rich-quick slogans

questions.explanation: Automation makes good defaults easier than relying on memory and mood.

wrongExplanations.c: Crisis-only attention is reactive and costly.
wrongExplanations.d: Hype slogans are not a control system.

questions.prompt: Before a large non-urgent purchase, what does the lesson recommend?

options.text: Buy immediately so you do not miss out
Pause and check budget fit, opportunity cost, and total financed cost if any
Finance it regardless of interest
Drain the emergency fund first

questions.explanation: A deliberate pause protects cash flow and values-based choices.

wrongExplanations.a: Urgency is often a marketing tactic.
wrongExplanations.d: Emergency funds are for true emergencies.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Investing Literacy, Risk, and Systems
quizzes.intro: Use the full lesson. Focus on investing concepts, insurance, mistakes, and durable systems—without guaranteed-return thinking.

questions.prompt: Which statement about investing is consistent with this course?

options.text: Diversification eliminates all chance of loss
Investing involves risk; diversification and time horizon matter; returns are not guaranteed
Hot tips are safer than learning fees and risk
Short-term rent money should be put in speculative bets

questions.explanation: Beginner literacy emphasizes risk, diversification, horizon, and fees—never guaranteed outcomes.

wrongExplanations.a: Diversification reduces some risks but not all losses.
wrongExplanations.d: Money needed soon should not take market risk lightly.

questions.prompt: Why do investment fees matter over long periods?

options.text: They do not matter at all
Costs compound against you and can meaningfully reduce results
Higher fees always guarantee higher returns
Fees replace the need for an emergency fund

questions.explanation: Even small ongoing costs add up over decades.

wrongExplanations.a: Fees are a real drag on outcomes.
wrongExplanations.c: Higher fees do not guarantee better performance.
wrongExplanations.d: Cash buffers and investing costs are separate issues.

questions.prompt: What is a sound way to think about insurance in a money plan?

options.text: Insure tiny losses and ignore catastrophic risks
Prioritize coverage that prevents financial disaster, then tune details carefully
Never buy insurance if you budget well
The cheapest policy is always best

questions.explanation: Insurance is risk transfer for ruinous events, not a substitute for every small expense.

wrongExplanations.d: Fit and coverage matter, not only price.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best matches lifestyle creep?

options.text: Automating more savings after a raise
Increasing spending automatically as income rises so savings never grow
Building a sinking fund for annual bills
Reviewing subscriptions quarterly

questions.explanation: Lifestyle creep absorbs raises into higher spending without intentional goal funding.

questions.prompt: What should you do when a message promises sure profits or overnight wealth?

options.text: Treat it as trustworthy education
Step back; treat guaranteed-return pressure as a warning sign
Invest emergency funds immediately to not miss out
Skip reading fees because urgency matters more

questions.explanation: This course explicitly rejects get-rich-quick and guaranteed-return marketing.

wrongExplanations.a: Guarantees are a red flag, not education.
wrongExplanations.c: Emergency money has a safety job.
wrongExplanations.d: Urgency often hides costs and risk.

questions.prompt: Which habit best turns finance knowledge into durable skill?

options.text: Reading tips once and never looking at statements
Tracking, planning, automating, reviewing monthly, and adjusting without shame
Comparing net worth publicly every day
Chasing a new strategy whenever markets move

questions.explanation: The core loop—track, plan, automate, review, adjust—builds stability over time.

wrongExplanations.a: Knowledge without review does not change outcomes.
wrongExplanations.c: Public comparison fuels anxiety more than systems.
wrongExplanations.d: Constant strategy hopping is usually behavior risk.
